# IMPRINT: opt-in latent memory policy, random weights and a CPU smoke

## Ticket Type

💡 Feature Request / Improvement

## Description

LeRobot has no IMPRINT policy. [Memory Without Curation: Learning Multi-Stream Latent Memory for Robot Policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14406) trains a multi-stream latent memory and then conditions a flow-matching action expert on it. The reference code is Apache-2.0 at [amazon-far/imprint](https://github.com/amazon-far/imprint).

Proposal: an opt-in policy type `imprint`, selected with `--policy.type=imprint`. Existing policy defaults stay as they are. `TinyFrameEncoder` is the image stem. It is a stand-in for DINOv3 and Wan 2.2, and its weights are this policy's own random initialization. Stage `memory` trains the memory decoder. `load_memory_weights` copies that memory into a joint policy and leaves the decoder behind. Stage `joint` trains the small flow-matching expert.

This is the architecture with random weights and a CPU smoke run, not a paper result.

### CPU smoke

Dry run on one Mac, `device=cpu`, public dataset `lerobot/pusht` episode 0 (161 frames, 1 episode). Batch size 2. Two optimizer steps per stage. PyAV decoded the video after TorchCodec failed to load.

| Stage | Learnable parameters | Step 1 loss | Step 2 loss |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| memory | 109325 | 2.083 | 1.746 |
| joint | 49210 | 2.218 | 2.436 |

Stage memory step 1 split: visual 0.528, action 2.052, proprio 0.880, progress 0.177. Step 2 split: visual 0.480, action 1.512, proprio 0.925, progress 0.096. Stage joint reports `loss_action` only.

The handoff loaded 76 memory tensors and skipped 42 decoder tensors. After the joint stage the expert is present and the decoder is absent. The copied memory tensor changed across the two joint steps. That shows the handoff is wired. It is not evidence that memory helps.

Two `select_action` calls returned finite actions of shape `(1, 2)`. `reset` cleared the chunk counts.

### Limits

- Two optimizer steps with random weights do not measure the paper. These losses are a Dry run.
- No RMBench, RoboCasa, or real-robot success rate is claimed.
- DINOv3, Wan 2.2, Pi0.5, and the Amazon-FAR checkpoints were not downloaded.
- The RoboCasa replay archive published with amazon-far/imprint `252ae09fcc2a94874fe0876d15142fe483ac553f` is not in this change.
- `chunkwise_wy` is not implemented. The checked path is the Python event scan.
- The paper training stack is Linux x86_64, Python 3.11, CUDA 12.8, and four 80 GB GPUs. That run was not launched.

## Context & Reproduction

Implementation and evidence: https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/5171

The pull request head is `fb0cc45b9a1c908c6b65b8cf9e9cf0ba39ab64c6`, rebased onto huggingface/lerobot `d9da92cfa8cf6d5df1e803d3baa7a9287bff099a`. The CPU smoke ran on the parent `6c13bfb5e23b2b69e24c6f4361ffb59b7930c522`. The later commit only aligns the README table for prettier. Local checks on that smoke commit:

- `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check` on the imprint package and tests: clean
- `uv run mypy src/lerobot/policies/imprint src/lerobot/policies/__init__.py`: no issues in 6 source files
- `uv run pytest tests/policies/imprint -q`: 20 passed

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [x] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

## Additional Info / Workarounds

The image stem is `TinyFrameEncoder`, a stride-2 convolution and a spatial mean. Paper-scale training, frozen DINOv3, Wan 2.2, and Pi0.5 weights stay out of scope.
